x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs. 3 is wrong: the CDS has no military command over the Service Chiefs (he chairs the Chiefs of Staff Committee).

st.2: The Hindi original was calligraphed by Prem Behari Narain Raizada.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Raizada calligraphed the English original; the Hindi one was by Vasant Krishan Vaidya.

st.3: It provided for direct elections on the basis of adult franchise.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the direct elections were on a limited franchise of property, tax and education, not adult franchise.

st.3: Article 329A was omitted by the 42nd Amendment.
st.2: Article 2A (Sikkim as an associate State) was inserted by the 36th Amendment and omitted by the 35th.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Art. 2A was inserted by the 35th and omitted by the 36th. 3 is wrong: Art. 329A was omitted by the 44th Amendment.

st.2: Restrictions under Article 19 may be imposed by executive order, without any law.
st.3: Parliament can curtail them by an ordinary law.
st.1: They are absolute, so the courts cannot judge the reasonableness of restrictions on them.

x: Only 4 is correct: Art. 17 binds private persons too. 1 is wrong: FRs are qualified and courts judge reasonableness. 2 is wrong: Art. 19 restrictions need a law. 3 is wrong: FRs can be curtailed only by a constitutional amendment.

st.1: A citizen of India may accept a title from a foreign State with the consent of the President.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: under Art. 18(2) a citizen shall not accept a foreign title at all.

st.3: A British citizen living in India can claim the freedom of trade and profession under Article 19(1)(g).
st.1: A company, as a legal person, can claim Article 19 in its own name.

x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: a company cannot claim Art. 19, though citizen shareholders may sue. 3 is wrong: Art. 19 is for citizens only.
Both are correct: the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 effectively decriminalised attempted suicide, and the BNS has no general offence for it.

st.2: Free legal aid is a Fundamental Duty of every citizen under Article 51A.

x: 1 is correct (Art. 48A and Art. 51A(g)). 2 is wrong: free legal aid is DPSP Art. 39A, not a Fundamental Duty.

st.2: A Bill is a Money Bill merely because it provides for the imposition of fines or penalties.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: under Art. 110(2) fines or penalties do not by themselves make a Bill a Money Bill.

st.2: An amendment abolishing a tax also requires the President's recommendation.
st.4: A State Bill restricting inter-State trade needs the previous sanction of the Governor.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: an amendment reducing or abolishing a tax needs no recommendation. 4 is wrong: such a State Bill needs the President's previous sanction (Art. 304(b)).

st.3: Amaravati was made the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh in 2026 by amending Section 8 of the Act.
st.2: The Godavari River Management Board manages the Srisailam project.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Srisailam is under the Krishna River Management Board. 3 is wrong: the amendment was to Section 5 (capital); Section 8 is the Governor's security responsibility.

st.3: C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected in September 2025 after Jagdeep Dhankhar died in office.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Dhankhar resigned in July 2025; he did not die in office.

st.2: At least 14 days' notice must be given, and the resolution must state the grounds of removal.
st.3: A casual vacancy must be filled within six months, and the new Vice-President serves only the rest of his predecessor's term.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: no grounds need be stated. 3 is wrong: there is no six-month deadline and the new VP gets a full five-year term.

st.2: While a resolution for his own removal is under consideration, he may exercise a casting vote.
st.4: The post has been vacant since June 2019 because the Constitution makes filling it optional.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: during his own removal resolution he has no casting vote. 4 is wrong: Art. 93 says the House 'shall' choose a Deputy Speaker; filling it is not optional.

st.2: The Lok Sabha may increase a Demand for Grant.
st.3: The Finance Bill is passed before the Appropriation Bill.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Lok Sabha may only pass, reject or reduce a demand. 3 is wrong: the Appropriation Bill comes before the Finance Bill.

st.1: The ordinance-making power is beyond judicial review.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: ordinances are subject to judicial review.
Both are correct: an ordinance lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles, and earlier if both Houses disapprove it.

st.3: The concept of judicial restraint developed in the United Kingdom.
st.2: The term 'judicial activism' was coined by Justice P.N. Bhagwati.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the term was coined by Arthur Schlesinger Jr. (1947). 3 is wrong: judicial restraint also developed in the USA.

st.1: A retired Supreme Court judge may plead in any High Court but not in the Supreme Court.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: a retired SC judge cannot plead in any court in India (Art. 124(7)).

st.3: Its recommendations are binding on the Union and the States.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: its recommendations are not binding.

st.3: The second Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted by the Supreme Court.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: KWDT-II (2004) was constituted by the Central Government under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, not by the Supreme Court.

st.4: Membership of Parliament for ten years is one of the qualifications for a member.
st.3: The Chairman must be a judge of a High Court or qualified to be one.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Chairman must have experience in public affairs; High Court judge is a qualification for a member. 4 is wrong: there is no MP qualification.

st.2: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are binding on the Union Government.
st.3: P.V. Rajamannar, Chairman of the 4th Finance Commission, held that the Union could turn its recommendations down without giving any reasons.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the recommendations are advisory. 3 is wrong: Rajamannar held that they should not be turned down without very compelling reasons.

st.2: In April 2019 the Supreme Court raised VVPAT verification to five EVMs per Lok Sabha constituency.
st.3: In ADR v. ECI (April 2024) the Supreme Court ordered a 100% count of VVPAT slips.
st.4: Symbol loading units need not be sealed or stored once the symbols are loaded.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the 2019 order raised verification to five EVMs per Assembly segment, not per Lok Sabha constituency. 3 is wrong: ADR v. ECI (2024) rejected 100% VVPAT counting. 4 is wrong: symbol loading units are sealed and kept for 45 days after the results.

st.1: The State Secretariat is the field agency that implements policies at the district level.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Secretariat is the policy apex; implementation is left to field agencies.

st.2: The occupancy rate was 112.7%, the highest being in Meghalaya.
st.3: Convicts made up about 73% of the inmates.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the highest occupancy was in Delhi (194.6%), Meghalaya being second. 3 is wrong: it is undertrials, not convicts, who made up about 73%.

st.3: The Central Information Commission is one of the organisations exempted under Section 24.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the CIC is the appellate information body, not a Second Schedule organisation.

st.3: Under Section 8(3), all exemptions lapse after 20 years, without exception.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: most exemptions lapse after 20 years, but those on sovereignty and security, Parliament's privilege and Cabinet papers (clauses a, c and i) do not.

st.2: It recommended that the Section 8 exemptions be read broadly.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Second ARC wanted Section 8 read narrowly.

st.1: It felt there was no need to amend Articles 355 and 356.
st.4: The phrase 'either on their request or otherwise' for deploying central forces originated with the Sarkaria Commission.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Punchhi wanted Arts. 355 and 356 amended. 4 is wrong: the phrase originated with the First ARC.

st.2: In the 2004 Lok Sabha election the Congress won no seat in Kerala for the first time as the UDF swept the State.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: it was the CPI(M)-led LDF that swept Kerala in 2004.

st.3: A person confined in prison may vote by postal ballot.
st.4: An overseas elector enrolled at the passport address may vote from abroad by postal ballot.
st.2: Under Article 324, a citizen aged 18 or above may be disqualified from voting for non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: adult suffrage and its disqualifications are in Article 326; Article 324 vests elections in the ECI. 3 is wrong: a person in prison cannot vote; only preventive detenus vote by post. 4 is wrong: an overseas elector must vote in person in India.

st.2: Parties must report every contribution above ₹20,000 to the CAG.
st.1: The cap on anonymous cash donations was cut from ₹20,000 to ₹2,000 by an Election Commission order in 2017.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the cut to ₹2,000 came through Budget 2017 (Finance Act), not an ECI order. 2 is wrong: contributions above ₹20,000 are reported to the ECI, not the CAG.

st.2: Its Inquiry Committee (1952) was chaired by Balwant Rai Mehta.
st.1: The campaign was started by the Planning Commission.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the campaign began in 1943, before the Planning Commission (1950) existed. 2 is wrong: the Inquiry Committee was chaired by V.T. Krishnamachari.

st.2: The Panchayat Samiti was to be an advisory body.
st.4: The Zila Parishad was to be the executive body.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 and 4 are wrong: the Panchayat Samiti was the executive body and the Zila Parishad advisory and supervisory.

st.2: Like the Autonomous District Councils, the Tribes Advisory Council has legislative and judicial powers.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the TAC is only advisory; legislative and judicial powers belong to the Sixth Schedule councils.

st.3: The Mandal Parishad President is directly elected by the voters.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the MPP President is elected indirectly by the MPTC members.

st.2: A vehicle tax is a compulsory tax of the Gram Panchayat.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the vehicle tax is optional.

st.2: The same amount was offered whatever the population of the Panchayat.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the incentive rose with population – ₹5 lakh below 2,000, up to ₹20 lakh above 10,000.

st.3: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 exempts strategic projects within 100 km of the coastline.
st.4: In August 2026 the Environment Ministry stated that the FRA has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II clearance.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the exemption is for strategic projects within 100 km of the international borders, not the coastline. 4 is wrong: it was the Ministry of Tribal Affairs that said so.

st.2: A project qualifies as a 'mega project' only on investment, never on the number of jobs.
st.3: The State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) is chaired by the Industries Minister.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: a project with 2,000 or more direct jobs is also a mega project. 3 is wrong: SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh was the first State to adopt Panchayati Raj, in 1959.
st.4: The Community Development Programme was launched on 2 October 1952 on the recommendation of the Balwantrai Mehta Committee.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Rajasthan was first; Andhra Pradesh followed in 1959. 4 is wrong: the CDP (1952) came first; the Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957) reviewed it.

st.3: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched on 2 October 2014.
st.2: AMRUT, the Smart Cities Mission and HRIDAY were launched on the same day, 25 June 2015.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: AMRUT, Smart Cities and PMAY-U were launched on 25 June 2015; HRIDAY came on 21 January 2015. 3 is wrong: the Jal Jeevan Mission dates from 15 August 2019; 2 October 2014 is SBM-Urban.

st.2: Its Chapter 1 is titled 'Saving Lives and Livelihoods'.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Chapter 1 is 'State of the Economy: Pushing the Growth Frontier'; 'Saving Lives and Livelihoods' was ES 2020-21's theme.

st.3: In the IMF World Economic Outlook of April 2026, India stayed ahead of Japan and the UK by nominal GDP.
st.2: In 2025, India became the fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP by overtaking Germany.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: India overtook Japan, not Germany. 3 is wrong: the April 2026 WEO placed India 6th, behind Japan and the UK.

st.2: Manufacturing absorbed most of the surplus farm labour.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: manufacturing failed to absorb surplus farm labour (the missing middle).

st.2: The income Gini (World Inequality Database) fell from 62 in 2004 to 52 in 2023.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the income Gini rose from 52 (2004) to 62 (2023).

st.3: The Finance Commission suggests these measures on the basis of the recommendations of the State Election Commission.
st.2: They concern measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of India for panchayats and municipalities.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the measures augment the Consolidated Fund of a State. 3 is wrong: they rest on the State Finance Commission's recommendations.

st.3: The Sixth Finance Commission was chaired by Y.B. Chavan.
st.2: The Fifth Finance Commission (1968) was chaired by P.V. Rajamannar.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the 5th FC was chaired by Mahaveer Tyagi; Rajamannar chaired the 4th. 3 is wrong: the 6th was Brahmananda Reddy's; Chavan chaired the 8th.

st.2: The performance grant is 20% and fully tied.
st.4: Issue of municipal bonds is an entry condition for the grants.
st.3: The rural share of local-body grants rises from 36% to 45%.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the performance grant is fully untied. 3 is wrong: it is the urban share that rises from 36% to 45%. 4 is wrong: municipal bonds are not an entry condition.

st.1: It operated after the Administered Pricing Mechanism was dismantled.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the Oil Pool Account operated under the APM and closed with it. 2 is wrong: the Finance Minister in 2002 was Yashwant Sinha.

st.2: Fertiliser subsidy is the largest subsidy.
st.4: Among the major subsidies, petroleum subsidy is larger than fertiliser subsidy.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: food subsidy (₹2,27,629 crore) is the largest. 4 is wrong: petroleum subsidy is far smaller than fertiliser subsidy (₹1,70,799 crore).

st.1: It can promote full employment but cannot influence economic growth.

x: 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: by shaping aggregate demand, fiscal policy supports both employment and growth.

st.1: Indirect taxes are generally progressive in nature.
st.2: Indirect taxes are generally non-inflationary.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: indirect taxes are generally regressive. 2 is wrong: indirect taxes raise prices and are inflationary.

st.2: GSTN was made fully government-owned by transferring all its shares to the Union Government alone.
st.3: An e-way bill is required only for inter-State movement of goods.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: in the fully government-owned GSTN the Centre and the States hold 50% each. 3 is wrong: e-way bills apply to intra-State movement too (above ₹50,000).

st.2: The GST concept was first used in Canada.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: GST was first used in France; India follows Canada's dual model.

st.2: Taking an open position on expected exchange-rate moves is called arbitrage.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: an open position on expected moves is speculation; arbitrage is buying where cheaper and selling where dearer.

st.1: Foreign investment in public-sector banks is capped at 74%.

x: Only 2 is correct: brownfield pharma FDI is allowed up to 74% automatic. 1 is wrong: the 74% cap is for private-sector banks; public-sector banks are capped at 20%. 3 is wrong: 100% FDI in trading of food products made in India is through the Government route.

st.3: The SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 kept QFIs outside the FPI framework.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 2019 Regulations unified FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs as FPIs.

st.3: It runs on IM-PDS, which was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development.
st.1: It started in August 2019 in all States at once.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: ONORC began in August 2019 in only four States. 3 is wrong: IM-PDS (2018) is the Department of Food and Public Distribution's.

st.2: MSP was abolished after India joined the WTO.
st.4: Bt brinjal, like Bt cotton, is approved for commercial cultivation.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: MSP was never abolished. 4 is wrong: Bt cotton (2002) is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation; Bt brinjal is under a moratorium.

st.3: Per Drop More Crop (micro-irrigation) continues to be a component of PMKSY.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Per Drop More Crop left PMKSY in December 2021 and is now under RKVY.

st.2: The Koneru Ranga Rao Committee (2006) was set up by the N. Chandrababu Naidu government.
st.3: Land distributed to the poor in AP has come mainly from ceiling-surplus land.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the committee was set up by the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government. 3 is wrong: distributed land came mainly from government (assigned) land.

st.1: It was created in SIDBI in 1995-96 with an initial corpus of Rs 2,000 crore.
st.3: Rural drinking water falls under its irrigation category.

x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the RIDF was created in NABARD, not SIDBI. 3 is wrong: rural drinking water is in the social-sector category.

st.2: Banks were asked to halt lending for PM Surya Ghar.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: banks were asked to lend for PM Surya Ghar, not halt it.

st.3: The blue box covers input subsidies such as fertiliser subsidy.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the blue box is production-limiting payments; input subsidies are amber box.

st.3: The 25% target of the National Manufacturing Policy was achieved by 2022.
st.2: The share of manufacturing has risen steadily to about 25% of GVA.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: manufacturing has stayed near 15-17% of GVA. 3 is wrong: the 25% target was missed.

st.3: Its loans are available only for manufacturing units, not for services or trading.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Stand-Up India covers manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities and trading.

st.2: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 gives residual AP a share of Hyderabad's tax revenue for ten years.
st.1: AP was bifurcated on 2 June 2014, and Telangana got 13 of the districts.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: residual AP had 13 districts; Telangana got 10. 2 is wrong: APRA 2014 gives AP no share of Hyderabad's tax revenue.

st.1: Its Chairman is the Governor.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Chief Minister chairs the APEDB.

st.2: Visakhapatnam is not one of the districts covered.
st.3: The package is a one-time grant of ₹50 crore per district.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Visakhapatnam is one of the three North Coastal districts. 3 is wrong: each district gets ₹50 crore every year, not once.

st.1: Tabling the Socio-Economic Survey before the budget speech is a constitutional duty.
st.3: CFMS (2018) stands for Centralised Fund Monitoring System.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: tabling the Survey is a convention, not a constitutional duty. 3 is wrong: CFMS stands for Comprehensive Financial Management System.

st.2: The 12th Pay Revision Commission for AP employees was set up by the Union Government.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the 12th PRC (due from 1 July 2023) was set up by the State Government, not the Union.

st.3: Capital outlay to GSDP ratio
st.2: Interest payments to capital outlay ratio

x: Only 1 is a standard sustainability ratio. 2 is wrong: the measure is interest payments to revenue receipts, not to capital outlay. 3 is wrong: capital outlay to GSDP measures the quality of spending, not debt sustainability.

st.2: In 2018, AP said the CAG had not rejected its utilisation certificates.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: AP said NITI Aayog, not the CAG, had not rejected its UCs.

st.1: The Centre bears the full cost of Polavaram, including its power component, from 1 April 2014.
st.2: The promised ten-year tax holiday for industry was implemented in full.

st.4: In Rythu Bazars, traders and commission agents sell the farmers' produce.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: in Rythu Bazars farmers sell directly to consumers, without traders or commission agents.

st.3: Veligonda is a lift irrigation project.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Veligonda is a gravity project.

st.3: It ranks 7th among States in industrial output, ahead of Tamil Nadu.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: AP's coastline is third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. 3 is wrong: AP is 7th, behind Tamil Nadu. 4 is wrong: coal surplus is not an AP endowment.

st.3: T&D losses rose from 9.32% in 2014-15 to 12.10% in FY 2024-25.
st.2: Farm pump sets get 9 hours of free night-time power, with APRAPSCom as the nodal agency.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the 9 hours of free power are given in daytime. 3 is wrong: T&D losses fell from 12.10% to 9.32%.

st.2: The Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 proposed five regional medical hubs and five university townships.
st.1: Multimodal logistics parks are identified at Visakhapatnam and Ananthapur under the Sagarmala Programme.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the multimodal logistics parks come under Bharatmala Pariyojana, not Sagarmala. 2 is wrong: the medical hubs and townships were proposed in the Union Budget, not the AP Budget.

st.3: Its Principal Bench is at Bhopal.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Principal Bench is at Delhi; Bhopal is a zonal bench.

st.4: Its centre is in the gaseous (plasma) state.

x: All four are correct: the Sun holds 99.8% of the system's mass, is 109 × the Earth's diameter, fuses hydrogen at ~15 million °C, and is gaseous (plasma) even at its centre.

st.3: Of the 15 moons added in March 2026, 11 belong to Jupiter.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: 11 of the 15 were Saturn's and 4 Jupiter's.

st.2: Absolute magnitude is the brightness a star would have at 10 parsecs.

x: All three are correct: lower magnitude means brighter, absolute magnitude is at 10 parsecs, and apparent brightness depends on size, temperature and distance.

st.2: Exposed metamorphic rock cannot weather into sediment; it can only melt into magma.
st.4: Enhanced rock weathering spreads crushed granite on farmland to lock carbon dioxide as bicarbonate.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: any rock type can become another, and exposed metamorphic rock weathers into sediment. 4 is wrong: enhanced rock weathering uses crushed basalt, not granite.

st.3: Stanford University made the first global map of continental mantle earthquakes.

x: All four are correct: a doublet is two similar independent quakes close in time and place; Caracas had one (M 7.1 and 7.5) in June 2026; Stanford mapped continental-mantle quakes; homoseismal lines join places of equal arrival time.

st.4: Anthromes are ecological units shaped by natural climate without human use.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: anthromes are shaped by sustained human use.

st.3: The Gulf of Kutch, with about 7,000 MW, is India's most potential tidal-energy area.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India's most potential tidal-energy area (about 7,000 MW) is the Gulf of Khambhat, not the Gulf of Kutch.

st.4: Waves carry water, not energy, across the ocean.
st.2: A rip current is a narrow, fast channel of water flowing away from the shore.

st.2: The Bihar and Bengal plains are divisions of the Ganga Plain.

x: Both are correct: the Ganga Plain comprises the Doab, Rohilkhand, Avadh, Bihar and Bengal plains.

st.2: Polavaram district was carved out of Anakapalli district.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Polavaram district was carved out of Alluri Sitharama Raju district, not Anakapalli.

st.2: Water is Entry 17 of the State List, subject to Entry 56 of the Union List.

st.2: The Sendai Framework has four priorities for action.

st.2: Its 10 new fishing harbours are being built under PMMSY.

x: All three are correct: AP gives about 30% of India's fish and 31% of shrimp exports, its 10 fishing harbours are under PMMSY, and the Blue Economy CoE is at Vignan's University.

st.2: The Coconut Development Board functions under the Ministry of Agriculture.

x: All three are correct: Commerce has five statutory boards, the Coconut Development Board is under Agriculture, and CRIJAF is at Barrackpore.

st.2: Cooperative mills dominate the North, especially Bihar.

x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the North has mostly private mills; cooperatives dominate in the South, especially Maharashtra.
